classification.difficultyReason: Derive the perimeter contribution of an attached square, then translate its side-length ratio into an area percentage.

content.prompt: Jim has a field in the shape of a square. He acquires an adjacent square field, which increases the perimeter of his field by $10\%$. Find the percentage increase in area of his field.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 22, lower right column beneath the stem
spec.description: An unlabelled large square with a smaller square projecting from an interior portion of its right edge near the top. The combined outline has no internal dividing line. Drawing coordinates express illustrative proportions only, not additional numerical givens. Source pale green decorative fill is omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: The acquired square shares its complete left side with part of the original square's right boundary. Adding a square of side s increases the external perimeter by 2s and the area by s squared.
spec.answerVisibility: No lengths, calculations or answers are supplied in the question diagram.

answer.short:
$4\%$ increase.

The perimeter gain is twice the smaller square's side, so its side is $20\%$ of the original side and its area is $4\%$ of the original area.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the original square's side length and $s$ the acquired square's side length. The shared side is internal, so the perimeter gain is $4s-2s=2s$.

$$\begin{align*}2s&=0.10(4x)\\2s&=0.4x\\s&=0.2x\end{align*}$$

The added area is the area of the smaller square.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase in area}&=\frac{s^2}{x^2}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase in area}&=\frac{(0.2x)^2}{x^2}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase in area}&=4\%\end{align*}$$
